name: Stubai Wasserfall
kurzbeschreibung: The mighty Stubaier Wasserfall plunges 80 m deep into a wild gorge—a natural spectacle for the whole family.
beschreibung: This entry describes the „Stubai Wasserfall“ as a natural spectacle in the municipality of Neustift im Stubaital: a waterfall with a drop of around 80 meters, several viewing platforms, a directly adjacent inn, and an excursion destination accessible year-round free of charge. The given coordinates are located in the municipal area of Neustift, the main town of the Stubai Valley at just under 1,000 meters above sea level, around 25 kilometers south of Innsbruck. Neustift is the second-largest municipality in Tyrol by area and a starting point for hikes to the Elfer. The Stubai Valley is known, among other things, for the Stubai Glacier and the WildeWasserWeg trail with its waterfalls. No further verifiable information about the described location is available here.
